reasoning: The underlying problem — detecting LLM sandbagging without weight access — is heavily studied, but the dominant high-performing methods are white-box (linear/instruction-pair deception probes reaching AUROC 0.96-0.999) or require weight modification (noise injection, arXiv 2412.01784). The confirmed black-box behavioral approaches I could pin to credible sources (the "Playing Dumb" LessWrong post and the "Comparative Analysis of Black Box Methods" Alignment Forum post) rely on accuracy shifts under casual-vs-formal question reframing and consistency/awareness probes, NOT on cheap generation-time traces. Multiple search summaries reference work investigating API metadata "such as token count, response time, and tokens per second" for sandbagging detection, suggesting this specific feature family has been at least touched, but I found no clearly attributed, credible paper using output-token-count + wall-clock latency + hedging-language features in a lightweight classifier evaluated by AUROC on instructed honest-vs-sandbag conditions — so that specific combination is unexplored to underexplored. Note a validity caveat the literature stresses: black-box detection is not adversarially robust (models can logit-match a weaker model), and system-prompt-instructed sandbagging is the easy case, so a positive result would have limited counterfactual weight.

evidence.title: AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations
evidence.summary: Foundational paper formalizing sandbagging; shows models can be prompted/fine-tuned to selectively underperform and emulate a weaker capability profile, explicitly noting detection is hard when evaluators only have black-box access. Establishes the problem the proposal targets is well-defined and studied.

evidence.title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models
evidence.summary: Standalone sandbagging detector that injects noise into weights and observes anomalous accuracy gains. Strong detection but requires weight modification, not pure black-box; an XGBoost classifier on resulting signals reached near-perfect accuracy on Llama-70b/Deepseek/Mistral-7b. Different mechanism from the proposed cheap behavioral traces.

evidence.title: Playing Dumb: Detecting Sandbagging in Frontier LLMs via Question Framing
evidence.summary: Black-box sandbagging detection using casual vs formal question framing; sandbagging produces >50% accuracy drop between framings. Uses semantic/contextual reframing and a threshold detector, NOT output token count, latency, or hedging features — so the proposal's specific cheap-trace angle is not covered here.

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Black Box Methods for Detecting Evaluation Awareness in LLMs
evidence.summary: Compares five black-box methods (binary test, probability estimation, user-motivation guessing, reasoning-trace analysis, log-prob analysis). None work well; none use generation latency, output token count, or hedging-language features. Confirms the behavioral-trace feature set proposed is not the standard black-box approach.

evidence.title: Building Better Deception Probes Using Targeted Instruction Pairs
evidence.summary: White-box linear/instruction-pair probes detect deception including sandbagging scenarios at AUROC 0.96-0.999, catching 95-99% of deceptive responses at 1% FPR. Represents the strong-but-white-box alternative; the proposal's contribution is doing this with only cheap black-box features, which these probes do not address.

evidence.title: Time Will Tell: Timing Side Channels via Output Token Count
evidence.summary: Shows output token count and response latency leak information about LLM outputs via timing side channels (e.g. output class, language). Demonstrates that token-count/latency are informative black-box signals in general, lending plausibility to the proposal but applied to a different task (side-channel info leakage, not sandbagging detection).
